solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A way of cooking swine over scattered ashes

indicators.note: the cur is laid over, covering, the jumbled letters

parts.note: a swine is a despicable person, as is a cur

indicators.note: ashes that are scattered are thrown about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe in which a pig is roasted over a bed of embers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' looks like the pig being cooked; it is a contemptible person, and 'over' means covering the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasseur is a French style of cooking, meat done in a mushroom, wine and tomato sauce, as in chicken chasseur.

clue.text: Catch trousers, making hole in suit

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it

indicators.note: making a hole in the word trousers knocks out its middle and leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone snags their trousers and tears a hole in their suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making hole in' empties trousers to its outer letters T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Henry initially admitted to strain in period at work

indicators.note: a letter admitted to a word is let inside it

parts.note: to strain flour or liquid is to sift it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Henry

explanation.surface: Henry, at first, is let in to ease the pressure during his working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H from Henry, and 'admitted to' puts it inside SIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is the stretch of hours a worker spends on duty, such as a night shift.

clue.text: Small space husband's given, tucking into nuts and cheese

parts.note: an em is a printer's space, the width of the letter M

indicators.note: the husband letter is tucked into the word for crazy

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mental

explanation.surface: A husband snacks on nuts and cheese in a cramped little room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, which fits the snack picture, but it puts the husband inside the word for crazy; 'given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss holey cheese, here in its alternative spelling with an H.

clue.text: Again go up wing on sports ground

indicators.note: the wing word is set on the ground word, placed after it in the answer

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a public sports field
a wing, like an arm or leg, is a limb

explanation.surface: A winger runs up the touchline of the playing field once more.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' would normally mean above, which would put the wing first; here it only means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclimb is to scale or ascend something a second time.

clue.text: Times secretary outside in storms needing alternative route

parts.note: times as in multiplication is by, as in three by four
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: the outside letters in the word storms are its first and last

explanation.surface: A newspaper's secretary, out in bad weather, needs another way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside in' takes the outer letters S and S from storms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road taking traffic round a town, a different way past it.

clue.text: Informally grill fish above Queen's Head

parts.note: the barb is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of Queen

explanation.surface: Fish is cooked on a grill above the head of a pub called the Queen's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' takes Q, the first letter of Queen's. The pub sign is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bar-B-Q is a casual spelling of barbecue, the outdoor grill, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Sexed-up ad involved duet

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A racy advert features a pair singing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the letters of SEXED-UP AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas de deux is a ballet dance for two performers, a duet in dance.

clue.text: Family member tabloid caught in the act?

indicators.note: caught as in heard by the ear, so the paper's name stands for a word that sounds the same

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
an act of Parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A relative is snapped by a red-top in the middle of something compromising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' turns the tabloid SUN into SON by sound; IN is as printed and LAW is the act. 'caught in the act' looks like the idiom for being found out.
explanation.definitionFit: A son-in-law is a daughter's husband, a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Religious movement's topics regularly cited in dull retrospective

definitions.note: the clue's 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the chosen letters are quoted inside the reversed word
looking back, so the word for dull is read backwards

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not glossy

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word topics

explanation.surface: A faith's main subjects are mentioned now and then in a boring survey of its past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of topics; 'retrospective' and 'cited in' read like a book review.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is a Chinese religious and philosophical tradition following the Tao, the Way.

clue.text: I'm surprised Carol on piano's forgetting lines

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that a carol singer at the piano has lost the words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts SING after P; the 's is 'has' and only a link. Corpsing is properly an actor breaking down laughing, which fits 'forgetting lines' loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre slang, corpsing is when an actor dries up or breaks into giggles and fluffs the script.

clue.text: Children, drawing with coloured fluid, start to illustrate European capital

indicators.note: drawing as in drawing back or withdrawing, so the word for children is pulled round backwards

parts.note: tots are small children
ink is the coloured fluid in a pen

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter, here of illustrate

explanation.surface: Kids sketching with paints begin to picture a capital city of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' reverses TOTS to STOT, and 'start to' gives I. 'European capital' wants a city such as Helsinki; it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Stotinki are the small coins of Bulgaria, a hundredth of a lev, so money in a European country.

clue.text: Perhaps Victoria will join son Brooklyn's neighbour

parts.note: Victoria is an example of a queen

explanation.surface: Victoria joins her son Brooklyn, as with the Beckham family.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria and Brooklyn suggest the Beckhams, but Brooklyn is the New York borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is the New York City borough that borders Brooklyn.

clue.text: Poet's private place to risk meeting maiden in environs of Harlow?

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the poet's name to the wordplay

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a private place
to bet is to risk money

indicators.note: the maiden letter goes inside, within the surroundings of, the film star's first name

parts.note: Jean Harlow was the 1930s Hollywood star
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A poet's private hideaway where he gambles on meeting a girl near the Essex town of Harlow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in environs of' puts M inside JEAN. Harlow looks like the Essex new town; it is the actress.
explanation.definitionFit: John Betjeman was Poet Laureate from 1972 until 1984, famous for gently comic verse.

clue.text: German agreed about ancient golf club being an exotic wood

parts.note: ja is German for yes
ca, short for circa, means about
the R and A, the Royal and Ancient, is the golf club at St Andrews

explanation.surface: A German nods along about an old golf club made from tropical timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews in Scotland, spelt out as R AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacaranda is a tropical tree whose fragrant hard timber is prized for furniture.

clue.text: Soldier lavishly spent ages recollecting service

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, gives a volunteer soldier
to blow money is to spend it extravagantly, so blew

indicators.note: recollecting looks back, so the word for ages is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a long age

explanation.surface: A soldier who splashed out recalls years of military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' reverses ERA into ARE. 'service' looks military; it is a set of dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a matching set of plates and dishes, all of which is tableware.

clue.text: Male witch seen during day in European city

indicators.note: the male and witch words are seen within the day's letters

parts.note: Tue is the abbreviation for Tuesday
he is the male pronoun
a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: A warlock is spotted in daylight in a continental city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male witch' reads as warlock, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hague is the Dutch seat of government, home of the International Court of Justice.

clue.text: Type of idyllic landscape having dark brown evergreen tree

parts.note: chocolate is a dark brown colour
box is an evergreen shrub or small tree used for hedging

explanation.surface: A pretty rural view with a brown-leaved evergreen tree in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate-box describes picture-postcard prettiness, like the old cottages once painted on sweet boxes.

clue.text: Senseless talk — Trump's mouth action that's typical of Donald?

indicators.note: the mouth of a word, like a river's mouth, is taken as its opening letter, here of Trump

parts.note: Donald Duck walks with a waddle

explanation.surface: The President's nonsense is described as the way Donald Trump carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald looks like Trump again; it is Disney's Donald Duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is nonsense, foolish chatter without meaning.

clue.text: Si tracks taxi, half of them leaving ranks

indicators.note: half of each of the words Si, tracks, taxi goes away, leaving the first half of each

explanation.surface: Si follows a cab, half the cabs leaving the taxi rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of them leaving' keeps S, TRA and TA, the first halves of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers or levels, as in the strata of society, so ranks or classes.

clue.text: Loose hair's found sticking to unknown wine

indicators.note: loose hair is untied and unruly, so these letters are let fall in a new order

parts.note: z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A stray hair turns up stuck in a glass of mystery wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' rearranges HAIRS to SHIRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiraz is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, also called syrah.

clue.text: Unspecified eye trouble, the latest to be given priority, that's stinging

parts.note: z is an unspecified quantity, an algebraic unknown

indicators.text: the latest to be given priority
indicators.note: the last letter of the eye trouble word is moved to the front

parts.note: a stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid

explanation.surface: An unnamed eye complaint, most recent first, that hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the latest to be given priority' moves STYE's last E to the front, making ESTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Zesty means sharp and piquant, with a tang that bites the tongue.

clue.text: City cook overcome by advance payment for short story

indicators.note: the city and cook letters are covered over by the payment word

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in advance in poker
EC is the postcode for the City of London
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A cook in the City is swamped by a payment in advance for a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome by' puts ECDO inside ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a brief amusing account of something that happened.

clue.text: Log some of military raids northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, backwards
some of the words military raids holds the letters within them

explanation.surface: A record of a few army raids heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' finds YRAID in militarY RAIDs, and 'northwards' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily record, like a ship's log of events.

clue.text: Did Labour once stray, backing Miliband Jnr?

parts.note: once means formerly, ago

indicators.note: backing means reversing, so the word for stray is read backwards

parts.note: to stray morally is to sin
Ed Miliband is the younger brother of David Miliband

explanation.surface: Did the Labour Party go astray in the past by supporting the younger Miliband?
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party from 2010 to 2015 over his elder brother David. 'backing' reverses SIN to NIS. 'Labour' looks like the party; it is toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to struggle and toil painfully, so labour hard over something.

clue.text: Sarah's heart is touched by rich old statesman

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, here inside Sarah

parts.note: rich food is fatty, fat

explanation.surface: Sarah is moved by a wealthy elderly politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes all but the outer letters of Sarah; 'is touched by' only sets the next piece beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yasser Arafat was the long-time Palestinian leader and Nobel Peace laureate, now dead.

clue.text: Georgia and Charlie are in line for bequest

indicators.note: the state and the letter are placed inside the line word

parts.note: a ley is an ancient straight line joining sites, a ley line
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Georgia and Charlie wait in line for an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' is the ley line, an imagined straight alignment of ancient sites.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left to someone in a will.

clue.text: Joe's actual mother revealed in letter

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the actual and mother words are shown inside the spelt letter

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
very means actual, as in her very words
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Joe's real mother is named in a letter he receives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence; it is the spelt-out name of N.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe, as in ordinary Joe or Joe Public, is the typical person in the street.
